newsitem.title: LEBANON: CGTL protest against south Lebanon union election.
newsitem.headline: CGTL protest against south Lebanon union election.

text.p: Lebanon's General Labour Confederation protested on Monday against what it said was police aggression during a union election in the southern city of Sidon.

Witnesses said police entered the Sidon branch of the CGTL on Sunday before voting began in regional council elections, confined journalists to a room in the building and took away 26 unionists to police headquarters.
Scuffles broke out after the journalists were confined for two hours and they said they heard shots and shouting in the building.
The leftwing Beirut daily as-Safir reported that at least three people suffered gunshot wounds in the shooting.

The detained unionists, who were released later in the evening, were members or supporters of an anti-government list of election candidates favouring CGTL chief Elias Abou Rizk, an outspoken critic of billionaire Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri.
The witnesses said the election continued after police removed the anti-government candidates and a 12-member list of Hariri supporters won.

"We reject the results of Sunday's elections carried out in an atmosphere of repression and call for new elections free of authorities' intervention," the CGTL leadership in Beirut said after a meeting on Monday.
"We strongly condemn the aggression practised against the leadership of south Lebanon unions," it said in a statement.

The Sidon election was the second of four CGTL regional council elections which Beirut newspapers have described as a fight between Abou Rizk and Hariri. They say Hariri is making a determined bid to oust Abou Rizk and his leftist CGTL leadership.
The new regional councils will elect a new CGTL national leadership when Abou Rizk's four-year term expires at the end of May.
The union of Lebanese reporters condemned the violence and said it was planning to take to court "those who have held or humiliated journalists or seized their equipment."
